title: Finite type quasi-coherent modules descend along fpqc coverings
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $F$ be a quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent; def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. If every tensor pullback $f_i^*F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], then $F$ is of finite type. There is no Noetherian or quasi-compactness assumption on $X$, and the index set may be infinite (or empty when $X$ is empty).

proof.text: For each affine open U of X, form the PreZeroHypercover of the original family. The quasi-compact part of hf gives QuasiCompactCover. Apply Mathlib QuasiCompactCover.exists_isAffineOpen_of_isCompact directly to hU.isCompact, obtaining n, indices a : Fin n -> I and affine opens V_j of Y_{a(j)} with union of their images equal to U. Hence V_j is contained in f_{a(j)} inverse-image U. No restriction of schemes or compactness of X is needed.

Set R = O_X(U), A_j = O_{Y_{a(j)}}(V_j), and g_j = f_{a(j)}.appLE U V_j. Each g_j is flat by the flat affine-section criterion. The finite product B of the A_j is flat by transport from its direct sum. To lift a prime p of R, use hU.isoSpec to find a point x of U representing p, then the covering equality to find y in some V_j mapping to x. IsAffineOpen.comap_primeIdealOf_appLE identifies the corresponding prime of A_j as lying over p. Pull it back through the coordinate evaluation B -> A_j. Its contraction to R is p, so R -> B is faithfully flat.

proof.text: For each j, transport ordinary-pullback quasi-coherence along tensorOrdinaryPullbackIso to the tensor pullback. The hypothesis hfinite and finite_sections_of_finiteType give finite sections on V_j. Apply exists_tensorPullback_affine_sections to the affine opens U and V_j and their containment. Compose its bijective R-linear map with tensor symmetry; its scalar-compatibility clause makes the composite A_j-linear. This gives a linear equivalence from A_j tensor_R F(U) to those finite section modules, hence finite generation of each tensor factor.

source.place: Tags 01I9 and 01IA; properties.tex Tag 01PB, lemma-finite-type-module; modules.tex Tag 01BG, lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent.

proof.text: For any finite family of R-algebras A_j and M, regard N_j = A_j tensor_R M as a B-module by coordinate evaluation. The identity is semilinear for the surjective evaluation map B -> A_j, so LinearMap.finite_iff_of_bijective makes each N_j finite over B. Module.Finite.pi then makes their product finite over B. TensorProduct.piLeft supplies the R-linear equivalence B tensor_R M -> product_j N_j, with coordinate formula (a tensor m)_j = a_j tensor m. Tensor induction verifies B-linearity: at pure tensors the equation is (ba)_j tensor m = b_j times (a_j tensor m); zero and sums follow by additivity. Upgrade the equivalence to B-linear and transport finite generation. All arguments allow the empty index type.

proof.text: Apply Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat to R -> B, using faithful flatness from step 2 and finite generation of B tensor_R F(U) from steps 3 and 4. Thus F(U) is finite over R for every affine open U.

proof.text: Use the opensRange of the members of X.affineCover; isAffineOpen_opensRange shows that each is affine and OpenCover.iSup_opensRange says they cover X. Apply clause (c) of quasicoherent_finite_type_affine with step 5 on every member. This gives finite type of F. The cover is arbitrary, not a finite subcover, and there is no compactness or Noetherian hypothesis. If X or the original index type is empty, the same proof applies.
